text: Good API design makes software easier to use and maintain. When building REST APIs, choose clear endpoints that describe resources, such as /users or /orders. Always return the correct status codes so clients understand what happened: 200 for success, 404 when something is not found, and 500 for server errors. Good documentation is essential because it helps other developers learn how to use your API quickly. Finally, use versioning, for example /api/v1/, so you can improve your API without breaking existing applications. These simple practices save time and reduce problems for everyone.
